title: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper
request: The Forgel Code client stops being only a set of one-shot, argument-driven wrappers. Opened without arguments it starts an interactive session in which the owner describes work in plain language, reads the agent's answers, follows the plan and the progress of tasks and releases, and accepts work or sends it back with remarks without leaving the session. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit. One-shot scripted usage and its machine-readable output remain unchanged, and the client stays thin: the model, the sandbox, independent checks, review and releases stay in the engine. The requirements below follow the existing feature document named by the owner and the client's documented contract; they are behaviour, not implementation.

audit.summary: The release delivers the interactive client and the successive redaction, localization, idle-refresh, retained-state and sensitive-action fixes, and the reported suites (369 tests at the final task) pass. One blocking gap remains in the redaction contract: the French password label is recognized only in its whitespace-separated form, so the common joined spellings are shown and retained unmasked. That can leak a password in an engine reply or error and violates the requirement that secrets and key material never appear in the session.

findings.issue: The redactor recognizes the French password label only as the whitespace-separated phrase `mot de passe`. Joined forms such as `mot_de_passe` and `mot-de-passe` are parsed as a single compound label whose segments (`mot`, `de`, `passe`) are not in `SECRET_WORDS`/`SECRET_WORDS_FOLDED`, so `_secret_label` returns false and `_phrase_end` (which compares the first label to `mot`) does not match. An engine reply or error such as `mot_de_passe=hunter2` or `mot-de-passe: hunter2` is therefore displayed and retained with the value intact, leaking a password and violating the requirement that secrets/key material never appear in the session. The task-11 review notes this residual but dismisses it; it is a data leak, not an optional improvement.
findings.suggestion: Treat the joined forms as the French password label: fold case and diacritics and accept whitespace, `-` and `_` between the words in `_secret_label`/`_phrase_end` (or normalize the label before matching). Add direct and session-level tests asserting that a value following `mot_de_passe`, `mot-de-passe` or `MOT_DE_PASSE` is absent from both the displayed and the retained text.
